sake.d: Japanese alcoholic beverage made from fermented rice; usually served hot

sakartvelo.d: a republic in Asia Minor on the Black Sea separated from Russia by the Caucasus mountains; formerly an Asian soviet but became independent in 1991

sakharov.d: Soviet physicist and dissident; helped develop the first Russian hydrogen bomb; advocated nuclear disarmament and campaigned for human rights (1921-1989)

sakkara.d: a town in northern Egypt; site of the oldest Egyptian pyramids

sakti.d: the female or generative principle; wife of Siva and a benevolent form of Devi

saktism.d: worship of Shakti as the wife of Shiva
